channel.project_pack_ref: Launch of Company-Wide Hybrid Onboarding Program

threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, success metrics, and 30-day onboarding journey map.

messages.text: Team, let's kick off the Hybrid Onboarding Program project. Our main goal is to roll out a standardized program in 21 days. First, we need to align on the scope and define what success looks like. I'm starting to think about T11, the success metrics. What are your initial thoughts? @54023 @84941 @173284

Great to get started. To help visualize the scope, I've put together a draft 30-Day Hybrid Onboarding Journey Map (A1) for T2. It's a starting point we can refine once the manager needs assessment from T1 is complete. Here's the link.
Thanks @434574. For metrics on T11, I suggest we track new hire satisfaction via surveys and the completion rate for mandatory modules within the first 30 days.
I'm looking at the journey map A1. For Day 2 'System Access Granted', does that mean just email and the HR system, or also things like the finance software?
Good question. The map currently covers core systems for everyone. We can add a note that department-specific software access is handled by the hiring manager, which we'll specify in their toolkit.
I agree with those metrics, @173284. Let's also add 'manager satisfaction with the process' to T11. It's critical for adoption.

So, to summarize and confirm our scope: we are building a standardized 30-day hybrid program covering core company policies and culture, with clear roles for managers and buddies, and allowing for optional department-specific modules. Is everyone aligned on this? This will be our decision D1.
Aligned. That scope is clear and achievable.
Yes, that works for me.
Great. Now for the 30-day journey map (A1). Based on the discussion, are there any other major concerns before we approve this version as our working draft for T2? This is for decision D2.
No concerns from me. I'll incorporate the small clarification on system access and it will be ready.
It looks ok to me now.
Excellent. Then we have our decisions. D1 and D2 are confirmed. I will start scheduling the manager interviews for T1 this afternoon to get that data quickly.

threads.thread_goal: Finalize core training content and facilitator guide for live sessions.

messages.text: Hi team, as part of T3, I've completed the first draft of the Core Onboarding Training Deck (A2). It covers the company overview, values, and key HR policies. I'd appreciate a review, especially on the compliance and policy sections. @434574 @173284. Link is here.
Thanks @54023. I'll review it this morning. The outline looks logical.
I checked the deck. On slide 12, the link to the employee handbook seems to be broken.
Thanks for spotting that, @84941! I've just fixed the link in the document.

I've reviewed the policy sections in A2. The content is accurate, but I recommend we add a specific slide on our Code of Conduct, maybe with a practical example to make it clearer for new hires. The rest of the content is very well done.

That's a great point, @434574. A scenario-based slide would be much more effective. I'll add that right now. With that change included, are we ready to sign off on the content for the core deck (A2)? This is for decision D3.
Yes, with that addition, I approve the content. (D3)

Perfect. Now, regarding the live sessions where this deck will be used. I propose we standardize them as 60-minute interactive meetings: 40 minutes to present the A2 content and 20 minutes for Q&A. This fits the constraints we have. This would be our decision D4. I'll then build the Facilitator Guide (A6) for T8 based on this format.
A 60-minute slot is a good duration, not too long and easy to schedule. I agree with that format.
Agreed. Let's confirm the 60-minute standard format for live sessions. D4 is locked in. Thanks for moving this forward so efficiently, @54023.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on manager toolkit, HR admin checklist, and tracking process.

messages.text: Hi all, I've created a draft of the Manager Onboarding Toolkit (A3) for T4. It includes a checklist, 1:1 agenda templates, and key talking points. @54023, could you please review for consistency with the training materials? @84941, this should align with the HR Assistant Onboarding Admin Checklist (A4) you're developing for T5. Link is in the project folder.
Of course. I'll review A3 against our journey map and training deck to ensure the messaging is perfectly aligned. I'll share my feedback by EOD.
Okay, I will look at A3. For my checklist A4, should I include the steps for ordering their laptop and phone?

Yes, please include equipment provisioning in A4. Let's keep all HR administrative tasks consolidated there. The manager's toolkit (A3) will just have a single item to 'Confirm new hire's equipment is set up and working'.

I've finished my review of A3. It's very clear and actionable for managers. My only suggestion is to add a small guide on 'Tips for selecting and supporting a buddy'. It's a key part of the experience. Otherwise, it looks ready.
That's a fantastic suggestion. I'll add that section. With that change, are we ready to approve the Manager Onboarding Toolkit (A3)? This is for decision D5.
The toolkit looks comprehensive and easy to use. I approve. (D5)
Great. Now, let's define the tracking process for T7. @84941, what are your thoughts on how to keep the Onboarding Completion Tracking Sheet (A5) updated?
I was thinking I can check with each new hire at the end of the week and then update the sheet A5.

A weekly manual check might create a lag, especially for mandatory compliance training. Could we make it more real-time? For instance, the trainer provides an attendance list right after a live session, and we can get automated completion reports from the e-learning platform.

I agree, a more systematic approach is better. Let's decide on the final process (D6): @84941, you will be the owner of the tracking sheet (A5). You'll update it within 24 hours of each live session using an attendance list from the trainer, and run a weekly report from the e-learning system for self-paced modules. How does that sound?
Yes, that is much clearer. I can follow that process. I will own updating A5. (D6)

threads.thread_goal: Lock in communication plan, FAQ, and rollout timeline for pilot.

messages.text: Team, we're in the final stretch. I've drafted the Onboarding Communication and FAQ Pack (A8), which covers T9 and T10. It includes announcement templates for managers and a detailed FAQ for new hires. Please take a look and provide feedback.
I went into the doc and added answers to questions I always get, like 'when is the first payday' and 'how do I request time off'. I hope that is okay.
That's excellent, @84941. Thank you for adding those practical questions to the FAQ for T10. It's exactly what we need.
I've reviewed the pack (A8). The messaging is clear and consistent with all our training materials. The FAQ is comprehensive. I think it's ready for approval.
The communication plan in A8 looks solid. Announcing to managers one week before the pilot is the right amount of lead time. I approve the pack.
Perfect. With everyone's input, let's officially approve the communication plan and FAQ pack (A8). This is decision D7.
Now for the final step: the pilot launch (T12). I propose we target the group of new hires starting in two weeks, on the 15th of the month. This gives us enough time to finalize all materials.
That date works perfectly. I'll have the facilitator guide and all session materials ready well in advance.

For evaluation, we'll deploy the Onboarding Feedback Survey Templates (A7) from T6 on Day 7 and Day 30. We'll also schedule a brief debrief with the pilot managers. So, to confirm decision D8: the pilot cohort is the intake on the 15th, with evaluation checkpoints at Day 7, Day 30, and a manager debrief. Are we all agreed?
The pilot plan is clear and robust. I'm aligned. (D8)
Okay, the 15th. I will prepare the list of new hires for that group.
Excellent. D7 and D8 are confirmed. We have a full plan for rollout. Let's focus on finalizing all remaining tasks this week. Great work, everyone.
